AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is strong: Q2 FY2026 showed revenue +16.6% YoY, EPS +21.8% YoY, net margin expanding 290bp to 27.2%, and balance sheet deleveraging (debt down from $94.8B to $82.7B, equity up ~60% from $66.8B to $106.5B). The franchise remains high-quality with 2.2B active devices, ~92% retention, and Services at $109B+ with ~70-75% gross margins. However, valuation is the binding constraint: at 35.5x PE the 2.8% earnings yield sits 165bp below the 10Y Treasury at 4.45%, leaving no margin of safety for a company that must sustain mid-teens growth to justify the multiple. The qualitative trajectory has deteriorated — WWDC AI announcements (reliance on Google Gemini, delayed rollout, 850M iPhones excluded) drew a sharply negative market reaction (-3.6% on June 8-9), Q3 FY2026 Services and China revenue both missed estimates with the stock falling ~4.5% after-hours, and a three-front regulatory assault (Supreme Court external payment ruling, EU DMA fine, DOJ antitrust) directly threatens the highest-margin Services segment. The CEO transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus adds execution uncertainty during this inflection. The stock is mid-range on its own PE history (30.3x-43.1x) and not expensive relative to itself, but the convergence of regulatory headwinds, AI execution gaps, China weakness, and leadership change means the near-term catalyst path is negative rather than positive. Pillar 3 (rerating chance) is a headwind: the Q3 Services miss and WWDC disappointment are dated, fundamental catalysts that argue against re-rating higher. Net: solid business, fair-to-full valuation, deteriorating qualitative trajectory — mildly positive but capped.

PE at 35.5x mid-range vs 30.3x-43.1x 365-day range; earnings yield 2.8% is 165bp below 10Y Treasury at 4.45% — no margin of safety

Three-front regulatory assault: Supreme Court App Store ruling (April 6, 2026) requiring external payment links ($2-4B commission revenue at risk), EU DMA €500M fine, DOJ antitrust suit
CEO transition: Tim Cook stepping down, John Ternus named successor (April 20, 2026) — first leadership change in 15 years during AI and regulatory inflection
Services segment $109.2B in FY2025 with ~70-75% gross margins — core of margin expansion thesis now facing regulatory headwinds
China headwinds: Huawei resurgence, AI regulatory approval requirements, Q3 China revenue miss; offset by India now 25% of iPhone production
